issues: the legal test for the internal relocation alternative under IRPA s. 97(1)(e) and what the RPD must establish to rely on it
the standard of review applied to RPD decisions on the internal relocation alternative under the Vavilov framework
whether the RPD must assess the reasonableness of internal relocation in light of the claimant's personal circumstances (means, family ties, health, age, gender) rather than mere possibility
whether the RPD erred in law by conflating the claimant's ability to relocate with an obligation to do so
the role and sufficiency of country conditions evidence in establishing that the alternative location is safe and that relocation is practicable
the allocation of the burden of proof regarding the internal relocation alternative
key_facts: RPD accepted the claimant's fear of persecution was genuine
RPD refused the claim on the basis that the claimant could have relocated to another city in the same country
the claimant is a woman who fled persecution in her home country
causes_of_action: judicial review of an RPD decision
candidate_statutes: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27, s. 97(1)(e)
Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7, s. 18.1
